transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-02
Start time: 14:00 PST
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Samira Patel (Redwood SE), Jordan Ruiz (Redwood SE), Mark Whitman (RiverMark, Network), Leah Gomez (RiverMark, Cloud), Priya Rao (RiverMark, Security), Caleb Moreno (RiverMark, CTO)

Summary:
Short intake call to understand RiverMark's constraints for private VPC-based access to Redwood Private. Primary asks: private endpoints vs VPC peering, egress/bandwidth limits, region residency (EU requirement for specific datasets), KMS/HSM integration for customer-managed keys, and a low-latency inference path for a real-time scoring product. Next steps were agreed (security docs, network templates, follow-up deep-dive).

Topics covered:
- Onramp options: Private endpoints (AWS PrivateLink) vs transit/peering
- Region constraints and data residency (EU vs US handling)
- Egress/NAT/IPS and bandwidth expectations for batch vs real-time workloads
- Authentication / key management and audit logs (KMS, HSM, SOC 2 concerns)
- Dedicated vs Hosted tradeoffs for SLA and predictable throughput
- Pilot provisioning and short-term benchmarks

Transcript body:
[00:00:00] Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intro from our side, Alex Chen AE, Samira Patel SE, Jordan Ruiz - we'll be engineering support.
[00:00:12] Mark: Hi, Mark here, network. Also Leah and Priya on from infra and security. We have Caleb the CTO in a bit.
[00:00:22] Alex: Great. The goal is to map your network requirements and any blockers for private deployment. Samira, you want to kick with the topology options?
[00:00:35] Samira: Sure, basically Redwood Private supports a couple patterns — private endpoints via AWS PrivateLink-like interfaces, VPC peering/transit gateway, or an on‑prem data plane via direct connect. For most customers we recommend private endpoints for minimal routing changes, but transit gateway is better for large-scale multi-VPC traffic.
[00:00:58] Leah: We were thinking PrivateLink so traffic never leaves AWS, but we need to understand how egress is handled and if we can keep EU customer data in eu‑west only.
[00:01:14] Samira: Right — region pinning is supported. We can deploy a control plane that’s global but the data plane for inference can be pinned to eu‑west-1 for those workloads. There are caveats about model variants and caching if you route to a different region; higher latency if model serving in a different region.
[00:01:35] Mark: On the egress side, our VPC has forced NAT through a central egress VPC for monitoring, so we’re worried about returning flows and source IPs. Does Redwood require static egress IPs?
[00:01:48] Jordan: For PrivateLink you won't need to egress to the public internet for inference egress; the endpoint is an ENI in your subnet and traffic is local. But for things like model updates or some telemetry, there may be outbound control plane calls; we document those domains and IP ranges for allowlisting.
[00:02:12] Priya: Can you annotate the domains? We need them for our proxy rules and SOC2 audit.
[00:02:20] Samira: Absolutely — we'll include a full allowlist. Typically it's a small set of control plane endpoints, and you can route via a proxy. We also support customer-managed KMS; Redwood can integrate with your KMS or you can bring keys for encrypting at rest.
[00:02:40] Leah: KMS integration is important for us. If we bring our own CMK, where does the key live and who rotates it?
[00:02:49] Samira: The key stays in your KMS. We integrate using cross-account grants; Redwood never copies the key material. Rotation is up to you; as long as grants remain valid the system will continue to decrypt. For HSM-backed keys, we have an enterprise setup — need an account sync with our security team.
[00:03:05] Mark: Good. Also network segmentation — we prefer minimal broad peering. Can you show a suggested subnet allocation?
[00:03:16] Samira: We'll propose a small /24 for the interface endpoints and an optional set of route table entries for peering. Note that if you use transit gateway, you'll need route propagation and potentially proxying through the egress VPC.
[00:03:30] Alex: One thing to flag, RiverMark mentioned real-time scoring — what's the SLO you need on p99 latency?
[00:03:37] Caleb (joining): Sorry, late. We’re targeting 150–250ms p99 for single-step scoring with 512 token-ish requests — anything higher starts to affect UX.
[00:03:49] Samira: That’s helpful. For that latency budget, we usually recommend Dedicated capacity co-located in the same region, with optimized kernels and smaller batch sizes. Hosted can hit high throughput but may add a bit more cold-path latency and multi-tenant jitter.
[00:04:03] Mark: If we go Dedicated, do we still use PrivateLink or is peering better?
[00:04:09] Samira: Both work. Dedicated is about compute tenancy. PrivateLink with Dedicated instances gives you the private connectivity and predictable capacity. Peering/transit gateway is useful if you want direct routing and you already manage TGW meshes.
[00:04:22] Leah: We're also constrained on IP space — we have a handful of /16s used across the org. If endpoints require unique IPs per service, that’s a challenge.
[00:04:34] Jordan: PrivateLink uses ENIs and consumes IPs in your subnets. The count scales with connections and AZs. For heavy scale, TGW can be more IP efficient but adds routing complexity. We'll produce an IP consumption estimate.
[00:04:50] Priya: Audit logs and traceability — can you stream audit logs to our S3 or Kafka?
[00:04:57] Samira: We support audit log export to customer S3 buckets or to your syslog/Kafka via a connector; retention policies are configurable. We'll highlight the fields included — request ids, token counts (aggregated), model version, and timestamps.
[00:05:12] Mark: Okay. One more note: some of our customers require data never leaves EU for certain datasets. How strict is the region pinning?
[00:05:20] Samira: It's strict — you can configure workloads per-tenant to stay in a region. The control plane might be in a different region but payloads for inference are pinned. We do recommend verifying model caching implications if you move between regions.
[00:05:36] Alex: There's often confusion about 'cache' — if the model KV cache is warm in US, and you pin to EU, you'll have a cold start until the EU node warms; that could add ~50–200ms depending on sequence length. We'll put numbers in the follow-up note.
[00:05:55] Leah: That's acceptable as long as predictable. For regulatory reasons we might want a dedicated EU instance.
[00:06:03] Samira: Dedicated in EU is available; we just need lead time to provision. Typical lead times for Dedicated nodes in a region are 2–4 weeks depending on capacity; short-term trials can be negotiated.
[00:06:16] Mark: Regarding firewalls, our infra team blocks outbound 0.0.0.0/0 and uses an egress proxy. Will the PrivateLink still work?
[00:06:26] Jordan: Yes, PrivateLink traffic is L2/L3 in VPC — you don't need outbound internet for inference. The control plane calls for management might need egress, but those can be proxied.
[00:06:39] Priya: On authentication — we want SAML SSO for the console and granular RBAC for key rotation ops.
[00:06:46] Samira: We support SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning, and Role-based access control with fine-grained roles. For customer-managed keys and HSM ops, we can gate actions to specific roles and record audit events.
[00:06:58] Caleb: About throughput — some jobs are bursty (spikes from ETL runs), others steady for real-time. How do you handle autoscaling without compromising latency?
[00:07:08] Samira: For Dedicated we offer configurable autoscaling policies and burst buckets. The runtime also uses smart routing to fall back to slightly cheaper model variants if capacity is tight, but you can disable automatic fallback for strict determinism.
[00:07:23] Mark: Can we get metrics per token cost and per-token latency breakdown for the demo tenant?
[00:07:29] Alex: Yes — Redwood Console will show token-level cost, latency per-route and per-model, and trace links. We'll share a sample dashboard.
[00:07:38] Leah: Bandwidth — do you have recommended egress rates for embedding-heavy workloads? We plan daily batch embedding jobs of ~20 million records initially.
[00:07:49] Jordan: That's heavy. For large batched embeddings we recommend batch jobs to a Dedicated ingestion pool with batching and async endpoints to optimize throughput. We'll include estimated GB/day and suggest using regional storage to stage.
[00:08:02] Priya: Encryption in transit — TLS is fine, but we need mutual TLS for internal links when possible.
[00:08:08] Samira: We support mTLS for private connectivity paths in enterprise setups. We'll document cert rotation and trust anchors.
[00:08:19] Mark: Any blockers around VPC peering across accounts? We have separate accounts per product line.
[00:08:25] Samira: Peering is account-agnostic but you need route table coordination. For multi-account setups Transit Gateway with route propagation is cleaner. We'll include diagrams for both.
[00:08:37] Alex: Quick note on troubleshooting — we've found customers with NAT hairpin issues when the egress VPC rewrites source IPs. If you have a central NAT, we'll need the NAT IP ranges to be allowlisted.
[00:08:50] Mark: We'll gather that.
[00:08:53] Caleb: Pricing question — if we commit to Dedicated in EU and maybe burst to US, how is that priced?
[00:08:59] Alex: Pricing is a mix of reserved capacity (monthly commit) and usage overage. We'll send a model-specific estimate based on your p99 and qps. Dedicated gives predictability and often lower unit price. We can model three scenarios in the follow-up.
[00:09:15] Leah: For the pilot, we'd like a short-lived environment in EU with a single model and a telemetry pipeline to validate latency and audit logs.
[00:09:22] Samira: Sounds good — typical pilot steps: share CIDRs and peering preferences, receive allowlist and endpoint diagram, provision short-lived Dedicated or Hosted-Private endpoints, run perf tests, iterate.
[00:09:36] Alex: Ok let's recap next steps and owners.
[00:09:40] Samira: I'll draw up a suggested subnet plan and private endpoint diagram.
[00:09:44] Alex: I'll send the SOC2 and KMS docs and a sample SAML/SCIM guide.
[00:09:49] Mark: We'll share current VPC CIDRs, NAT IPs and a short list of the security controls we need to validate.
[00:09:55] Priya: Also add the compliance questionnaire — we run one internally before procurement.
[00:09:59] Alex: Will do. Anything else?
[00:10:03] Mark: No, looks good.
[00:10:06] Caleb: Thanks, excited to move forward.
[00:10:10] Alex: Thanks all, we'll follow up by Wednesday with artifacts and schedule the network deep-dive.

(Transcript truncated — remainder was Q&A and quick scheduling logistics.)
